title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples & Ops Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook standardizes how we author, review, publish, and operate developer-facing documentation for Redwood Inference: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues and fixes. The goal is to make documentation fast to produce, easy to consume, and reliable as a first-line support resource.

Scope
-----
Applies to all engineering and developer experience (DevEx) contributors who produce documentation under the eng-developer-experience Confluence space and the public docs site. This includes: SDK reference guides (Python/JS/Go), quickstarts, example apps, REST and SDK API examples, docs-site runbooks, and the canonical top issues knowledge base.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
- Reduce time-to-first-success for new developers (measured by drop in "first API call" support tickets by 30% over six months).
- Ensure every quickstart has a working CI-verified example and test.
- Keep SDK-guide coverage parity within 7 days of any API surface change.
- Maintain docs-site availability SLO: 99.9% for the docs CDN and automated deploy pipeline.

Standards and conventions
-------------------------
- Tone: technical, concise, and example-driven. Use second-person ("you") for how-tos.
- Formatting: Use Confluence headings, short intro, bullet lists, numbered steps, and pipe tables for configs.
- Filenames: lower-case, dash-separated, ending with -YYYY.json (internal storage).
- Code blocks: Provide minimal end-to-end examples; prefer SDK+REST pairings.
- Ownership: Every doc must have an explicit owner (owner_team) and at least one reviewer.

Repository and docs-site flow
----------------------------
1. Author locally in Markdown or Confluence draft.
2. Place example apps in the repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devx-examples (branch: docs).
3. CI job: .github/workflows/docs-ci.yml runs linters, builds examples, and publishes artifacts.
4. Deploy: redwoodctl docs deploy --env prod triggers the atomic docs-site publish.

Docs CI pipeline (summary table)
| Stage | Purpose | Owner | Failure threshold | Recovery action |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| lint | style + link checks | devex | fail on errors | fix and re-run |
| build | compile site, static assets | devops | fail | rollback to last good build |
| examples-test | run example apps + smoke tests | eng-infra | fail | open PR to fix examples |
| publish | upload to CDN | devops | fail | retry and alert #docs-deploy |

SDK Guide template (required fields)
- Title
- Short summary (1-2 sentences)
- When to use (intent)
- Installation (pip/npm/go install) with supported version matrix
- Quick authenticated example (complete request -> response)
- Error handling examples and retry guidance
- Advanced usage: batching, streaming, function-calling (if applicable)
- Migration notes for breaking changes
- References and related pages

Example: Quick Python SDK install + request
```python
# Install
# pip install redwood-inference==1.4.2
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.text.generate(model="rw-moderate-1", input="Write a haiku about latency.")
print(resp.output_text)
```
Notes: include minimum reproducible example; include environment variables and local dev defaults.

Quickstarts and templates (required deliverables)
- Minimal quickstart (3-5 steps): show sign-up, API key, first request.
- Full quickstart (15-30 minutes): SDK + REST example, small sample app, CI snippet, and deployment checklist.
- Template repos: one per language (python-quickstart, js-quickstart, go-quickstart) in devx-examples.

Quickstart checklist (author)
1. README with purpose and duration estimate.
2. Prereqs: API key, recommended model, supported SDK version.
3. Working example with test script (./test.sh).
4. CI integration (.github/workflows/quickstart.yml).
5. License and contributing notes.

API examples guidance
- Provide both HTTP and SDK examples for common flows: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, and streaming.
- Use realistic prompts and model names from the model catalog.
- Include example responses and typical token counts.
- Document rate-limit behavior and recommended backoff: 429 -> exponential backoff with jitter; max retry 3.

Example: REST curl for text generation
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-moderate-1","input":"Summarize the following: ...","max_tokens":150}'
```

Docs-site operating procedures
------------------------------
Publishing process
1. Merge PR to main/docs branch after 2 approvers from devex or a product owner.
2. CI runs docs-ci; tests must pass.
3. DevOps on-call (rotating) verifies preview environment within 15 minutes.
4. redwoodctl docs deploy --env prod is executed by devops-oncall.
5. Post-publish smoke tests run. If failure, rollback to previous build and open incident under oncall-and-incident-response.

Rollback criteria
- Broken examples (more than 5% sample tests failing).
- Site build errors causing 5xx for >1 minute.
- Missing or malformed SDK reference pages after publish.

Monitoring and SLOs
- Docs CDN availability: 99.9% monthly. Alert if availability < 99.95% in 1-hour window.
- Deploy success rate: 99% for automated publishes.
- Example run success: >95% in CI.
Alerting: PagerDuty "docs-deploy" for publish failures and #docs-deploy Slack channel for non-urgent ops.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (living list)
-------------------------------------------------
1) "Invalid API Key / 401"
- Symptom: HTTP 401 or SDK UnauthorizedError immediately after onboarding.
- Canonical fix: Verify the key in the account console, ensure no leading/trailing spaces, check header name 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>'. If using environment variables, confirm export.
- Owner: customer-success + eng-developer-experience.

2) "Slow first token latency" (cold-start)
- Symptom: first token latency > 2s for ephemeral instances.
- Canonical fix: Document expected cold-start behavior for hosted models; recommend connection pooling and warmup calls. For Dedicated customers, recommend pinning model variants and keep-alive.
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

3) "429 Rate limit / retry behavior"
- Symptom: intermittent 429s under short bursts.
- Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff with jitter; server-side recommend: 50 requests/sec per API-key for rw-moderate-1 as baseline; adjust per customer. Add client-side throttling.
- Example retry snippet (JS):
```js
async function requestWithRetry(client, payload) {
  let attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 3) {
    try {
      return await client.text.generate(payload);
    } catch (e) {
      if (e.status === 429) {
        await sleep(Math.pow(2, attempts) * 100 + Math.random() * 100);
        attempts++;
        continue;
      }
      throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries hit');
}
```

4) "Model mismatch / unexpected outputs"
- Symptom: app sees different outputs after a deploy or model alias change.
- Canonical fix: Pin model versions in client config and use rollout policies for canary. Provide migration notes in SDK guides.

5) "Embedding drift / vector mismatch"
- Symptom: similarity scores change after quantization or model changes.
- Canonical fix: Recompute baseline embeddings for the canonical dataset; document embedding versioning and quantization profiles.

Canonical fixes must include: symptom, quick triage steps, owner, rollback/mitigation steps, and links to related runbooks. Keep this list in Confluence and mirror a short version in the public docs troubleshooting section.

Runbook: handling a docs-site publish failure
1. On CI failure: look at logs in artifacts/docs-build; triage build error.
2. If preview failed post-merge: revert PR and notify authors.
3. If production failure post-deploy: run redwoodctl docs rollback --to-last, create incident, and notify #docs-deploy and pager-duty.
4. Postmortem: owner prepares a 72-hour incident summary and publishes to oncall-and-incident-response/incident-review.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- DevEx Docs owner: Aisha Patel (devex@redwood.ai) — owner for standards and review process.
- DevOps on-call: see eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts roster.
- Examples repo owners: eng-developer-experience team (team@redwood.ai).
- Escalation: if issue is customer-impacting, follow support-process and involve customer-success.

Appendices
---------
A. Example docs CI job (excerpt)
```yaml
name: Docs CI
on: [pull_request, push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install
        run: ./scripts/install-docs-deps.sh
      - name: Run linters
        run: ./scripts/lint-docs.sh
      - name: Run example tests
        run: ./scripts/test-examples.sh
      - name: Publish preview
        run: ./scripts/publish-preview.sh
```

B. Useful commands
- redwoodctl docs deploy --env preview
- redwoodctl docs deploy --env prod --dry-run
- redwoodctl docs rollback --to-last

C. Template labels
- Use labels: docs, quickstart, sdk, example, retention-policy.

D. Change log template (required in PR body)
- Summary of change (1-2 lines)
- Why this change improves developer experience
- Backwards-incompatible changes (if any)
- Test plan and CI results

Document maintenance
--------------------
- Quarterly review: owner schedules a doc audit every 90 days.
- On API change: SDK owners must update SDK guides within 7 calendar days.
- After incidents: include learnings and doc updates in the postmortem within 72 hours.

If you have questions about this playbook or need a template scaffold, ping #devex or email devex@redwood.ai.
